issues.actual: scripts/enemy_agent.gd rebuilds and sorts the complete fusepoint_enemy group inside _separation_safe_velocity(), then invokes that admission path multiple times per navigation cycle for every active enemy. At the same time, the main scene runs RuntimeQualificationProbe in PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, deep-calls mission/roster/weapon state and periodically scans the complete scene tree for audio players. With 18 active enemies these are credible CPU hitch hot paths and must be profiled on a native renderer; the llvmpipe collector result cannot attribute the user's stutter to their computer.

open_issues.acceptance: A representative native-renderer before/after capture reports raw frame times, one-percent low, hitch count, CPU/GPU attribution, and named script hot paths with 3, 5, 10, and 18 active enemies. Enemy separation is computed once from a cached stable roster per physics cycle, QA instrumentation performs no per-frame deep state snapshot or scene-wide scan in ordinary play, and AI behavior/spacing remains unchanged. llvmpipe evidence is recorded only as collector evidence.
open_issues.actual: scripts/enemy_agent.gd rebuilds and sorts the complete fusepoint_enemy group inside _separation_safe_velocity(), then invokes that admission path multiple times per navigation cycle for every active enemy. At the same time, the main scene runs RuntimeQualificationProbe in PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, deep-calls mission/roster/weapon state and periodically scans the complete scene tree for audio players. With 18 active enemies these are credible CPU hitch hot paths and must be profiled on a native renderer; the llvmpipe collector result cannot attribute the user's stutter to their computer.
open_issues.expected: Ordinary gameplay performs bounded enemy steering and lightweight production work per frame; deep QA snapshots run only on demand or at a bounded debug sampling cadence.
open_issues.next_action: Capture native-renderer CPU/GPU profiler evidence, remove duplicate peer scans and sorts, and gate or sample QA-only deep observation.

blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `clean_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Burn down the three host-active combat_readability issues with bounded source repairs and same-loop black-box plus white-box retest paths while preserving the verified clean boot, input, renderer tuple, viewmodel profile, ordinary mission flow, and non-selected backlog issues.

diagnosis.root_cause: Loop 77 left three closure-ready defects on independent authoritative surfaces: success terminal presentation can coexist with late enemy damage/death feedback, enemy replay restore can compare against stale or mismatched route-reservation state for rift-c-09 and emit a Godot ERROR, and the retained combat-feedback matrix still preserves duplicate cleanup while failing to retain authoritative kill/enemy_death rows for Alpha and Bravo branch resolution.

stop_conditions: All three host-active issue ids are assigned exactly once and no deferred issue receives a current-loop disposition.
Developer self-validation shows no candidate-owned Godot ERROR after the exercised replay/restore branch.

Developer self-validation shows terminal success has bomb_defused victory presentation with no health-zero or death-feedback state, while terminal failure still executes bomb_detonated damage exactly once.
Developer self-validation shows Alpha and Bravo retained feedback rows include enemy_death or kill plus required companion families, with duplicate counts remaining zero.

strategy.rationale: Convergence mode and stagnation require a materially different repair pass from prior cleanup/tuning attempts. Treat each active issue at its authoritative producer boundary: terminal state gates damage before presentation, roster restore owns reservation identity before actor application, and branch combat resolution produces real enemy death/kill events instead of only retaining whatever rows happen to appear.

code: Run the project/source validation available to the Developer harness after edits and fix any parse or typed-GDScript errors in changed files.
Source-inspect changed call paths for event-id ownership, duplicate suppression, restore epoch handling, and release-build guards on tester_* actions.
runtime: Use Godot MCP after edits: ordinary boot/deployment smoke, captured mouse movement, W/A/S/D movement, R reload-only, F6 reset-only, and late runtime-log read after active callbacks.

Retest `tester_terminal_success_prepare`/`advance` and `tester_terminal_failure_prepare`/`advance` in the same runtime generation with runtime_state, terminal presentation snapshot, player snapshot, damage feedback state, enemy roster combat-enable state, and final runtime logs.

Retest replay/checkpoint/F6/fresh mission restore with `rift-c-09` and all 18 enemies sampled for stable identity, reservation receipt, transform, alive/health/ammo state, grounded occupancy, and absence of candidate-owned ERROR entries.

Retest Alpha and Bravo encounter prepare/commit/fire/advance sequences and capture `CombatFeedbackMatrix.retained_rows()`, duplicate counters, HUD combat-feed rows, enemy death/cleanup state, and immutable event ids.
visual: Capture focused gameplay screenshots for success victory without red death overlay, failure detonation with intended damage presentation, and Alpha/Bravo kill-feed/death feedback rows in the PRD-style tactical HUD.

Maintain the inspected PRD visual reference hierarchy: restrained top-right kill feed, readable lower HUD, no broad opaque debug rectangles, no bare `Enemy killed` label, and no narrative/feedback element covering reticle or combat silhouettes.

done_when: `tester_terminal_success_prepare` followed by `tester_terminal_success_advance` reaches `mission_state=bomb_defused` and the victory branch with player health above zero, no `combat_death_locked`, no active death feedback, no active enemy attack authorization, and no queued enemy shot that can apply afterward.

The success branch emits a structured receipt showing combat freeze, player damage rejection reason, enemy shot cancellation count, and terminal event id before `TerminalPresentation` becomes visible.

The failure fixture still reaches `mission_state=bomb_detonated`, applies the single terminal explosion damage event exactly once, drives the intended death feedback chain, and enters failure result only after the terminal presentation/video path permits it.

Replay, checkpoint restart, Home/new mission, and F6 clear the success/failure terminal latches without leaving player input, damage immunity, enemy combat disable, HUD damage state, or terminal presentation state stuck across runs.
tasks.instructions: Repair the success terminal authority boundary so successful defusal atomically disables enemy combat and player damage intake before any victory presentation or result page can observe the state. Do not create a second health authority or mask the problem in UI; make the existing mission, shell, player, roster/enemy, and terminal presentation controllers agree on one terminal event id and one combat-freeze receipt. Keep the bomb_detonated failure sequence intact and separately test it so the success fix does not suppress legitimate terminal explosion damage.
tasks.title: Fence Success Terminal Damage

done_when: Replay/reset using the same branch that previously failed completes without any Godot ERROR containing `Restore reservation mismatch for rift-c-09` or equivalent candidate-owned restore backtrace.

`rift-c-09` and every other roster actor retain stable id, region, role, route_slot, transform, alive/health/ammo state, activation state, grounded occupancy, and full-capsule clearance after replay, checkpoint restore, F6 reset, and fresh mission.

Restore snapshots use one explicit reservation source of truth per epoch: either the saved reserved slot is reapplied transactionally before actor comparison, or the roster recomputes and records the new reservation then updates the actor and receipt consistently. A stale vector mismatch must not be hidden by deleting validation.

Restore failure receipts remain fail-closed for real identity, region, role, route-slot, floor-support, collision, or occupancy defects, and no enemy is allowed to continue from a default transform inside authored geometry.
tasks.instructions: Repair the replay/checkpoint enemy restore transaction around reservation state. The current failure is not a spawn-position tuning task; make `mission_controller.reset_for_replay`, `enemy_roster.apply_restore_snapshot`, and `enemy_agent.apply_checkpoint_snapshot` agree on how reserved_position and route reservations are saved, restored, recomputed, validated, and committed for each restore epoch. Preserve full occupancy/occlusion safeguards and stable enemy identity, especially for `rift-c-09`.
tasks.title: Fix Enemy Restore Reservations

done_when: After ordinary deployment input, `tester_encounter_alpha_prepare`, commit/fire/advance, and `tester_encounter_bravo_prepare`, commit/fire/advance, `CombatFeedbackMatrix.retained_rows()` contains branch-local `enemy_death` or kill-family rows for both Alpha and Bravo.

Each retained kill/death row joins immutable event id, enemy authority/death state, animation or death pose, HUD combat-feed presentation, cleanup/collision/navigation shutdown, and companion player_shot plus enemy_shot_resolved or player_damage rows where applicable.

`MissionFeedbackController.duplicate_event_count`, combat feedback duplicate channel count, and terminal duplicate submit count remain zero; cleanup does not delete the required death/kill branch evidence.

The repair is producer-side: branch advancement or combat resolution must submit the canonical enemy death/kill event through the existing roster/mission/HUD feedback path, not fabricate a bare Label, debug row, synthetic UI-only kill notice, or duplicate cleanup-only receipt.

Ensure Alpha and Bravo prepared encounter resolution actually emits and retains canonical enemy death or kill evidence, then have the matrix join HUD, animation, cleanup, mission, and combat rows under immutable event ids.
